Subject: Please reopen: PR #812 changed the default wavelength frame

I did read the changelog. I have now traced the offset to a default change in PR #812, rather than a problem with my wavelength calibration.

In 2.4.3, LineList.__init__ defaulted to wave_frame='air'. In 2.5.0, it defaults to wave_frame='vacuum'. My optical spectra are calibrated in air, so using the same inputs and config after upgrading now pairs air-calibrated data with vacuum rest wavelengths unless I explicitly set the frame.

Near H-alpha, the vacuum/air wavelength ratio is approximately 1.00028, consistent with the downward redshift offset I reported, roughly 83 km/s. Explicitly restoring the air setting fixes the offset for my data.

For anyone finding this thread with the same issue, the workaround for air-calibrated spectra is:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Set the frame to match your data; this is not a recommendation to use 'air' for every dataset.

“Works fine for me” does not test this particular regression without checking the wavelength convention and configuration. Data already using vacuum wavelengths, or radio data where this optical air/vacuum mismatch would not be the same test, would not establish that the old optical workflow is unchanged. m_okonkwo also reported a possible offset above, which warrants investigation rather than closing the thread.

I am frustrated that this was marked solved and attributed to my calibration without establishing the cause. I spent two days investigating that suggestion, including unnecessarily re-reducing arc-lamp calibrations for 40 spectra. Asking whether I had “actually read the changelog” was dismissive, especially when the relevant entry says only “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812).” That does not communicate a change to a scientifically significant default.

Please reopen this thread. Could the maintainers add an explicit line to CHANGES.md documenting the air-to-vacuum default change and the workaround, and consider a warning when wave_frame is not explicitly set? That would make this much easier for other users to diagnose.
